feedback.problem: What is the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨{t}^{4},\,{t}^{2},\,4t⟩$ at the point $P(1,1,4)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(1,1,4)$ on the given curve. We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨1,\,1,\,4⟩ \\ ⟨{t}^{4},\,{t}^{2},\,4t⟩ & =⟨1,\,1,\,4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the respective components gives the system

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}{t}^{4}=1 \\ {t}^{2}=1 \\ 4t=4.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equality, we get $t=1.$ This value satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, the point $P(1,1,4)$ is at the tip of $r(1).$  

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t)⟩ \\  & =⟨4{t}^{3},\,2t,\,4⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =⟨4(1)^{3},\,2(1),\,4⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,2,\,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(1)‖ & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36} \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at $P(1,1,4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(1)}{‖{r}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}⟨4,\,2,\,4⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{3},\,\frac{1}{3},\,\frac{2}{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
